explanation: It happened on a TV special celebrating Motown, his old record label. The gliding step itself, which dancers called the backslide, was decades old.

claims.text: Michael Jackson first performed the moonwalk on television during a performance of Billie Jean.
Jackson did not debut the moonwalk on television during Beat It, Thriller or Human Nature.
Jackson's televised moonwalk debut came on a TV special celebrating Motown, the label he had recorded for with his brothers.
The backslide, the dance step behind the moonwalk, was performed by dancers decades before Jackson made it famous.

evidence.restatement: The televised debut was in Billie Jean, so it was not during Beat It, Thriller or Human Nature.
The special was Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever, celebrating Motown, the label the Jackson 5 recorded for.
Dancers were doing the backslide, the step behind the moonwalk, decades before Jackson made it famous.
Jackson's first televised moonwalk came in Billie Jean on the Motown 25 special (taped March 1983, aired May 1983).

claimResults.note: Rival test: I know of no earlier televised Jackson moonwalk. Dancer Jeffrey Daniel of Shalamar showed the glide on British TV around 1982 and is said to have taught it to Jackson, but that was not a Jackson moonwalk. High-risk, knowledge only: counts only with check A's external evidence (9.9).

evidence.restatement: The Motown 25 debut was in Billie Jean, not in Beat It, Thriller or Human Nature.
Motown 25 was a television tribute to Motown, the label Jackson started on with his brothers.
The backslide glide was an established dance trick long before 1983.
